fatigue.detail: Plain rolled bottom flange; welded attachments are checked separately in the detail register.

notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 4 simply supported 45-ft bays, W36X529 girders, two 40-ton cab cranes, bearing on the steps of the existing stepped columns (lower W33X221, upper W14X211) over the lower shafts' crane-side flanges, with top-flange ties to the upper shafts, the rail, bearings and end stops; the stepped columns are checked as two-shaft columns with their existing load effects (effective lengths from a buckling analysis), with the step's local checks, and the existing sidewall rod bracing takes the crane longitudinal forces. The flexible plate cannot pass as sized (tie sizing ratio tie-slip with no slip resistance (the bolt tension reaches the slip limit) for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars on the same saddle, each bar taking half the force. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 0.625 in each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The unstiffened lower web fails J10.2/J10.3 under the upper shaft's inner flange (Lower web · local yielding under the upper inner flange (J10.2)): a stiffener pair under the inner flange (J10.8), fitted to bear on the cap, the thinnest plate passing the stiffener checks. The existing 0.5 in step fillets fail Category F throat fatigue (step-weld-fatigue 1.66, no bearing credit for an unfinished cap): built up in the field to a 0.875 in leg (new work, AWS D1.1 Clause 11). At the step the tie runs only to the upper shaft's inner face (17.56 in from the girder web), where the sized paired flat bars exceeds its sizing ratio tie-move-root-fatigue (6.97 > 1.00): the existing column is not resized; the checks report the tie. New-steel remedies: a longer tie to a new stub or stand-off on the upper shaft, or a different tie type.

No compact W meets every sizing target; the closest: screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 1.40, vertical deflection 0.58, lateral 0.98 and rail-head movement with twist 1.11 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 113 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W36X487: tips ratio 1.82 > 0.85; lateral deflection 1.08 of the limit > 0.9; rail-head movement with twist 1.25 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios. The closest section is within the limits but not the sizing margins: …

Assumed existing lower shaft for a 40-ton crane (W30X173 to 15 t, W33X201 to 30 t, else W33X221; a fictitious example to be replaced with the survey). At the step the tie runs only to the upper shaft's inner face (17.56 in from the girder web), where the sized paired flat bars exceeds its sizing ratio tie-move-root-fatigue (6.97 > 1.00): the existing column is not resized; the checks report the tie. selections.designed: Pair of plates 0.88 in × 7.25 in, 0.37 in fillets; existing step fillets built up to 0.88 in
selections.reason: The unstiffened lower web fails J10.2/J10.3 under the upper shaft's inner flange (Lower web · local yielding under the upper inner flange (J10.2)): a stiffener pair under the inner flange (J10.8), fitted to bear on the cap, the thinnest plate passing the stiffener checks. The existing 0.5 in step fillets fail Category F throat fatigue (step-weld-fatigue 1.66, no bearing credit for an unfinished cap): built up in the field to a 0.875 in leg (new work, AWS D1.1 Clause 11).

Weld-on clip bases on the top flange are an AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1 attachment, Category D: the estimated top-plate range 27.03 ksi (rated-lift crane moment without impact plus the top-flange lateral bending under the side thrust) at all 500,000 cycles exceeds F_SR = 16.39 ksi (ratio 1.65, the project's all-cycle method). Bolted clamp plates leave holes for pretensioned bolts (item 2.2, Category B), as AISC DG7 and AIST TR-13 allow.

selections.designed: paired-bars, closest; tie to be designed by hand
selections.reason: Top-flange tie not resolved at the column step: at the step the tie runs only to the upper shaft's inner face (17.56 in from the girder web), where the sized paired flat bars exceeds its sizing ratio tie-move-root-fatigue (6.97 > 1.00) (configurator estimates), and neither the horizontal slotted tie plate nor the other flange tie type passes there. fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
